key_insight: BRIDGE pairs prostate biopsy whole-slide images across three preparation stages to support research on AI-based virtual staining and related imaging methods.
clinical_relevance: Gleason annotations enable research on whether virtual staining preserves information relevant to prostate cancer classification and grading.
method: Collect 869 prostate biopsy slides from 169 patients at one oncology centre in Poland.
Digitize each slide in paraffin, after deparaffinization, and after H&E staining.
Provide de-identified images in native scanner format with slide-level Gleason scores.
evidence_signal: The dataset contains 2,607 whole-slide images; the abstract reports no model performance or clinical validation results.
watch_item: Single-centre sourcing may limit generalizability, requiring validation across institutions and imaging workflows.
paper_title: The BRIDGE dataset: paired brightfield whole-slide images of prostate core-needle biopsies in paraffin, after deparaffinization and H&E staining
